responses.content:
Done. `/app/main.py` now implements an exhaustive state-space exploration of the buffered machine:

- **State**: shared memory bytes plus per-thread (program counter, FIFO store buffer, observation list), explored iteratively with a visited-set so duplicate states are explored once.
- **Transitions**: `store` appends to the thread's buffer; `load` reads each byte independently with youngest-own-buffer-store forwarding (partial forwarding supported), assembling little-endian; `fence`/`xchg` are enabled only with an empty buffer (`xchg` atomically reads shared memory, records the old value, writes the new one); any thread's oldest buffered store can drain to memory at any time, including after the thread finishes.
- **Termination**: all PCs exhausted and all buffers empty; distinct `(reads, memory)` outcomes are collected into a set, emitted as `{"outcomes":[...]}` with one JSON line per input line.

Validated by the 3 public smoke examples, 400 randomized cross-checks against an independent brute-force path enumerator (covering partial forwarding, blocked fences/xchg, drains-after-exit), and max-bound stress cases (3 threads / 10 instructions / 8 bytes) — worst observed runtime ~9 ms per request.
